Issue Title: [FEATURE] Plugin Protocol Definition

Description:
# Overview
Create the new `Plugin` Protocol that will serve as the primary abstraction for high-level agent features, replacing `HookProvider`.

**Parent Issue**: #1636

---

## Problem Statement
The current `HookProvider` naming doesn't clearly communicate its purpose as a mechanism for high-level agent features. The `Plugin` terminology is more intuitive and widely understood in the industry.

## Proposed Solution
Introduce a new `Plugin` Protocol with clear semantics for extending agent functionality.

---

## Implementation Requirements

Based on clarification discussion and repository analysis:

### Plugin Protocol Definition
- **Location**: `src/strands/plugins/plugin.py` 
- **Decorator**: Use `@runtime_checkable` for runtime isinstance checks
- **Properties**:
  - `name: str` - Identifier for the plugin
- **Methods**:
  - `init_plugin(self, agent: Agent) -> None | Awaitable[None]` - Initialize the plugin with an agent
  - Support both sync and async implementations (follow `HookCallback` pattern)

### Protocol Shape
```python
@runtime_checkable
class Plugin(Protocol):
    """Protocol for objects that extend agent functionality.
    
    Plugins provide a composable way to add behavior changes to agents.
    They are initialized with an agent instance and can register hooks,
    modify agent attributes, or perform other setup tasks.
    
    Example:
        ```python
        class MyPlugin:
            name = "my-plugin"
            
            def init_plugin(self, agent: Agent) -> None:
                agent.add_hook(self.on_model_call, BeforeModelCallEvent)
        ```
    """
    name: str
    
    def init_plugin(self, agent: Agent) -> None | Awaitable[None]:
        """Initialize the plugin with an agent instance.
        
        Args:
            agent: The agent instance to extend.
        """
        ...
```

> **Note**: The `agent.add_hook(callback, event_type)` method is available from PR #1706 which will be merged with this implementation.


### Testing Requirements
- Unit tests only (per parent issue #1636 decisions)
- Test Protocol behavior with both sync and async implementations
- Follow existing test patterns in `test_registry.py`:
  - Use pytest fixtures for mocks
  - Use `@pytest.mark.asyncio` for async tests
  - Use `unittest.mock.AsyncMock` for async callbacks

---

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Plugin Protocol is defined with `name` property and `init_plugin` method
- [ ] Both sync and async `init_plugin` implementations are supported (return type: `None | Awaitable[None]`)
- [ ] `@runtime_checkable` decorator is applied
- [ ] Plugin is exported from `strands.hooks`
- [ ] Plugin is exported from top-level `strands` package
- [ ] Unit tests verify Protocol behavior with both sync and async implementations
- [ ] Docstrings follow Google style with examples

---

## Technical Notes
- Use `Awaitable[None]` return type annotation to support both sync/async (same pattern as `HookCallback`)
- Plugin is intentionally separate from HookProvider (no inheritance relationship)
- No integration tests required per parent issue decisions

## Dependencies
- PR #1706 (add_hook convenience method) - will be merged together

## Design References
- [Design Document](https://github.com/strands-agents/docs/blob/main/designs/0001-plugins.md)
